source_hypotheses.required: Odd positive v_p(r), positive nonzero physical pole input, and the existing general-preparation finite hypotheses.
source_hypotheses.constructed: Same input r and b=42r(1+N)^2 with the new nested chain.
source_hypotheses.justification: Opposite coefficient parity gives descent; finite depths make N integral and W a unit on the required support.

constructed_objects.required: The actual rational coefficients of f(H),f(S-P), and Re(k_H w_S).
constructed_objects.constructed: All four coefficients and the same proxy remain; only eight norm-node coordinates are rearranged.
constructed_objects.justification: check_chain reconstructs their defining rows, inverse powers, nonzero guard, physical input and preparation consumer.

index_domain_coverage.required: Every rational solution in soundness, every integer input in completeness, every consumed prime outside {2,3,5,7,13,17}, and the final shared primary progression.
index_domain_coverage.constructed: Same root indices and detector data; stronger but finite local preparation, with 3^1064 dividing nonzero a-1.
index_domain_coverage.justification: The actual input polynomial excludes negative odd contacts. Finite scalar conditions precede root/scale selection and contact primes; the existing Pi^44 progression is retained.

transition_maps.required: Compatible normalization, square absorption, conic maps and diagonal decoding.
transition_maps.constructed: Scalar coefficient rho=42r remains distinct from physical b=rho W^2. New compiled conics and E=2130 diagonal factors are reconstructed.
transition_maps.justification: W>=1 and rho>0 justify the retained absorption and conic zero branches. Every diagonal factor and row divisor is nonzero. The norm replacement itself is justified by soundness/completeness, not witness equivalence.

limiting_object_identity.required: The scalar proxy theorem must apply to the points and index quotient consumed by the height argument.
limiting_object_identity.constructed: Both f(H) and f(Q) have positive coefficients at p before applying the trace theorem; Tproxy=((a-1)/h)U0 with U0 a p-unit.
limiting_object_identity.justification: The split-41 case is retained. This gives v_p(a-1)>=31 for the same nonzero scalar index. No limiting point replaces an actual witness.

coefficient_conventions.required: Q(sqrt(2)) coefficients, normalized rational p-valuations, unchanged exception set, and an integer quartic fixing X.
coefficient_conventions.constructed: kappa=r^-15, y=Tproxy/r^16; root coefficients r^-1 and r^-16; inner coefficients 1 and r^-15; E=2130.
coefficient_conventions.justification: All divisions use existing nonzero r. Original finite compiler, conic and diagonal checkers replay the result exactly.

local_conditions.required: Both formal places for the proxy, scalar order 31, and attainable finite completeness conditions.
local_conditions.constructed: Strict proxy depth exceeds (963/32)R. For p|r, all five leaves can be at depth >=16R+1, giving N depth >=16R+2.
local_conditions.justification: Odd R gives noncancellation at every node; integer valuation gives 31. The source permits arbitrary additional finite depth after fixing H, so Tproxy depth >=32R+1 is attainable.

exceptional_cases.required: Zero leaves, split primes including 41, chart identity exclusions, and all pole zero branches.
exceptional_cases.constructed: Zero leaves use infinite valuation; original H and Q guards retained; conic positivity retained.
exceptional_cases.justification: No new denominator or preparation specialization is used. The original nonzero shifted-point guard and both-place proxy argument are retained.

downstream_consumption.required: Scalar, Lucas and input contradictions with the actual height constants and local orders.
downstream_consumption.constructed: Order 31 yields c^415>(4H)^992 at c>=2*3^1064; order 45 retains the Lucas margin b^143>(24H)^360; order 12 retains the final input contradiction.
downstream_consumption.justification: The exact checker verifies all three margins, and PROOF.md connects them to each unchanged consumer. The smaller even anchor imposes only a weaker finite divisibility in completeness.

historicalDisposition: Prior norm, proxy, preparation, anchor and height arguments read; restricted earlier searches do not establish an optimum. No priority claim.
